slot.brief: A string fixed at both ends vibrating in a given harmonic; ask how the frequency changes when tension and vibrating length are both altered by given factors.

stem: A string fixed at both ends vibrates in its third harmonic. Its tension is reduced to one-ninth of its original value, while its vibrating length is reduced to half. The ratio of its new frequency to its original frequency is

verdicts.working: For the same harmonic, f = n/(2L)√(T/μ). Hence f_new/f_old = 2√(1/9) = 2/3.

working:
$f_n=\dfrac{n}{2L}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$
$\dfrac{f'}{f}=\dfrac{L}{L'}\sqrt{\dfrac{T'}{T}}$
$=2\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{9}}=\dfrac{2}{3}$

Independent check: For the same harmonic, f = n/(2L)√(T/μ). Hence f_new/f_old = 2√(1/9) = 2/3.
